sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian usually marks plural nouns with -k. The form of the noun may change before the suffix.

Notice mind pairs naturally with a plural noun — a barátok mind itt vannak — while sok, néhány and több all insist on a singular noun instead. Hungarian's quantity words don't follow one single rule, so it's worth learning each one's number behavior individually rather than assuming they all work like English 'many/some/more'.
